name: Loo
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020 (ms.). An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, 4th ed., entry '296. Loo'
sources.note: Entry gives names Shúṇóṇ-North / Shúṇóṇ-South, location, 8,000 (1992 est.), 'Adamawa: Bikwin group. Source(s) Kleinewillinghöfer (1992)'; no linguistic references (no grammar/phonology lines).

sources.citation: Norton, Russell & Nlabephee Othaniel. 2020. The Jen language cluster: a comparative analysis of wordlists. Language in Africa 1(3): 17-99. doi:10.37892/2686-8946-2020-1-3-17-99
sources.note: Comparative phonology of ten Jen-cluster varieties incl. Loo of Galdemaru and Loo of Waamura (Table 1 p. 18; Burak-Loo lexical similarity 88-92%). Sec. 3.3 Tone p. 43: 'High, mid, low, falling and rising tones were noted.' The words stress/accent/prominence do not occur anywhere (0 hits).

sources.citation: Idiatov, Dmitry, Mark Van de Velde, Tope Olagunju & Bitrus Andrew. 2017. Results of the first AdaGram survey in Adamawa and Taraba States, Nigeria. Slides, CALL 47, Leiden
sources.note: No Loo, Burak or Bikwin content (0 hits).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 records for looo1238 (languoid JSON, langdoc, Burak-Loo bura1270 and Bikwin-Jen bikw1235 family pages)
sources.note: All four MEDs for Loo are 'wordlist_or_less' (Norton & Othaniel 2020; Othaniel 2017; Kleinewillinghöfer 1996; Kleinewillinghöfer 1994); no grammar, sketch or phonology of Loo is recorded.

sources.citation: Adelberger, Jörg & Roger Blench. 2026. The peopling of the Muri Mountains, Northern Nigeria: evidence from linguistics and ethnography. Afrikanistik-Aegyptologie-Online. doi:10.18716/OJS/AAEO/2026_12031
sources.note: Sec. 3.2.3.5 Loo, p. 17: settlement, ~8,000 speakers, sections Shungo and Taadam; no phonology. The three 'stress' hits are non-linguistic ('stressful', 'stressing their claim').

sources.citation: Adelberger, Jörg. 2024. The Burak (same series). Ramsgate: Mandaras Publishing. 61 pp.
sources.note: Ethnographic; language paragraph = classification only; nothing on stress (0 hits).

sources.citation: Adelberger, Jörg. 2024. The Loo: a collection of ethnographic and historical data from fieldwork 1989-1993 (Ethnographic and Historical Profiles of the Peoples of the Muri Mountains - The Southern Groups). Ramsgate: Mandaras Publishing. 41 pp.
sources.note: Ethnographic profile; p. 1 classification only ('The Loo [ldo] language is part of the Bikwin-Jen sub-group'); p. 2 two sections Shuŋo and Taadam with 'dialectical differences'; glossary pp. 33-35 partly tone-marked (dàn káp, ìllè). No phonology, nothing on stress (0 hits).

sources.citation: Oppong Peprah, Miracle. 2023. Number marking strategies in Burak. Slides, 2nd Adamawa Conference, Paris, 15 Sept 2023 (LLACAN AdaGram)
sources.note: Sister variety Burak [bys] (Kleinewillinghöfer: Burak and Loo 'speak variants of one single language'). Slide 6 'General Features': nine vowels; syllable shapes (C)V(V), CV(V)C; 'Tones: Two level (H, L) with a downstep high tone (ꜜH)'. Nothing on stress; no Loo data.

sources.citation: Norton, Russell. 2019. Comparative phonology of the Jen languages. Slides, 1st Adamawa Conference, Mainz, 9-11 Sept 2019
sources.note: Wordlist correspondence tables with a Loo column; nothing on stress or tone rules.

sources.citation: Othaniel, Nlabephee Kefas. 2017. A phonological comparative study of the Jen language cluster. BA thesis (Glottolog: MA, 83 pp.), Theological College of Northern Nigeria, Bukuru / University of Jos
sources.note: Segment-level comparison (consonant/vowel inventories, cognate sets) with Loo data collected at Loo Dara (Shoŋɔ dialect; Tadam and Shoŋɔ named as the two Loo dialects). No tone or stress section; 0 hits for stress/accent.

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 2011/2015 (addenda 2019). Bikwin-Jen Group. Adamawa Languages Project web page, JGU Mainz; and LLACAN AdaGram Burak page (2026)
sources.note: Classification only: 'Burak and Loo, two distinct ethnic groups, speak variants of one single language. They can converse without any problem.' AdaGram: before Oppong Peprah's Burak project (2022) 'very little was known about the language'; Kleinewillinghöfer 2015 and Norton & Othaniel 2020 'both provide short wordlists'. Nothing on prosody.

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 1995/2015 (ms.). Bikwin-Jen: comparative wordlist (Swadesh 100). Adamawa Languages Project, JGU Mainz
sources.note: Tone-marked wordlist with two Loo columns (LOg = Loo [shʋŋɔ] of Galdemaru; LOw = Loo [shʋŋɔ] of Waamura); no prose on prosody; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Oppong Peprah, Miracle. in progress (CNRS Thèses internationales, LLACAN, since 2022). PhD dissertation / grammar of Burak [bys] (sister variety; Burak and Loo 'speak variants of one single language')
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only first-hand descriptive work on the Burak-Loo language; a phonology chapter would be the first place a stress/accent statement (or its explicit absence beside the two-tone system) could appear; the 2023 slides already give the tone system.
